{'role': 'user', 'content': [{'tool_use_id': 'toolu_01PnPtkAW1jjSQgxkFxbAvQY', 'type': 'tool_result', 'content': "1\t# `transport/` — enforced conservation gateway (salvaged, unwired)\n2\t\n3\tAn earlier, **independent** GEMS direction: instead of reconstructing the\n4\tGem infrastructure from evidence (`../src/gems/`), this builds the one thing\n5\t`conservation_kernel` says a library cannot provide for itself — an enforced\n6\ttransport boundary.\n7\t\n8\tSee [`PROVENANCE.md`](PROVENANCE.md) for where it came from, what was changed\n9\tto land it, and its gaps (no unit tests; not wired into the package).\n10\t\n11\t## The idea\n12\t\n13\t`conservation_kernel` verifies typed transformations but cannot stop a\n14\tdownstream process from ignoring a rejection. `ConservationGateway`\n15\t(`gems_transport/transport.py`) is that missing choke point:\n16\t\n17\t- a Gem's output is an untrusted **proposal**, never an accepted artifact;\n18\t- the gateway resolves the input artifact from **its own** accepted-artifact\n19\t  map, not from whatever the request claims;\n20\t- only `submit()` can promote a candidate, and only if the kernel accepts it;\n21\t- everything downstream (`Pipeline`) only ever sees accepted artifacts.\n22\t\n23\t`experiments/` is a deterministic corpus of 20 attack types\n24\t(`AttackType`, `AdversarialGem`) that each try to smuggle an unauthorized\n25\tstatus/origin/authority change past the gateway, plus a control path that\n26\tbypasses it.\n27\t\n28\t## Layout\n29\t\n30\t```text\n31\tgems_transport/\n32\t  transport.py       ConservationGateway, GatewayReconstruction\n33\t  pipeline.py        Pipeline — only forwards accepted artifacts\n34\t  contracts.py       GEMS/0.1 wire contracts (proposal/record/decision/result)\n35\t  registry.py        GemRegistry allow-list, append-only TransformationLedger\n36\t  artifact.py        re-exports the kernel Artifact model + lineage refs\n37\t  tie_adapter.py     TIE integration point (raises TIEIntegrationMissing)\n38\t  reference_gems/    BaseGem + researcher/reviewer/summarizer/requirements/\n39\t                     architecture + AdversarialGem\n40\texperiments/\n41\t  corpus.py          synthetic TIE source, human-approval fixture\n42\t  attacks.py         run_hostile_corpus, control_outcomes\n43\t  run_experiment.py  writes results/initial_run.json\n44\t```\n45\t\n46\t## Run\n47\t\n48\t```bash\n49\tcd transport\n50\tPYTHONPATH=/path/to/conservation_kernel/src:. python3 -m experiments.run_experiment\n51\t```\n52\t"}]}

Gem Registry & Routing**\n- System has specialized Gems, each with bounded roles and capabilities\n- A **Router** looks up which Gem can handle a requested capability\n- Routes deterministically (currently: first alphabetical match with the capability)\n\n**2. Workflow Coordination**\n- **WorkflowCoordinator** orchestrates multi-step execution\n- Takes an artifact and a capability request\n- Routes to appropriate Gem, executes the work, collects results\n- Tracks: task ID, execution state, artifact history\n\n**3. Provenance Preservation**\nEach artifact carries immutable metadata:\n- **Origin**: who created it (HUMAN, AI, JOINT, UNCERTAIN)\n- **Epistemic Status**: how confident (EXPLICIT, INFERRED, UNKNOWN, CONFLICTED)\n- **Authority**: what authority it claims (OBSERVATION, ANALYSIS, PROPOSAL, HUMAN_AUTHORIZATION)\n- **Parent IDs**: lineage trace to source artifacts\n\n**4. Governance Enforcement**\n- **HandoffValidator**: ensures handoffs between Gems preserve provenance\n- **GovernanceValidator**: blocks any artifact that loses its provenance\n- **Cognitive Continuity constraint**: AI-originated material cannot be labeled as human authorization without explicit human action\n\n**5. Evidence Integration (TIE)**\n- Adapts external evidence packages into the artifact model\n- Preserves unknown/uncertain provenance for unrecovered schemas\n- Maintains evidence linkage through the workflow\n\n---\n\n### **Key Invariants**\n\nThe system enforces five core constraints:\n\n1. **Role boundaries** — Gems have explicit, bounded capabilities\n2. **Provenance immutability** — metadata survives every transformation\n3. **No silent authority escalation** — AI proposals cannot become "human authorized" automatically\n4. **TIE linkage** — evidence remains traceable through the workflow\n5. **Structured results** — execution returns metadata (task ID, status, integrity, verification) not just output\n\n---\n\n### **Concrete Example**\n\n```\nInput: TIE_PACKAGE (external evidence)\n  ↓\nTIE Adapter converts to Artifact (marks origin=UNCERTAIN, authority=OBSERVATION)\n  ↓\nRouter: "I need analysis_capability"\n  ↓\nAnalyst Gem receives artifact, produces recommendation\n  ↓\nHandoffValidator checks: is provenance intact? The Router doesn\'t know about Provenance. The Validator doesn\'t know about capability routing.\n\n---\n\n## **Why This Matters**\n\n**Orthogonal infrastructure means:**\n\n| Aspect | Implication |\n|--------|------------|\n| **Independent failure modes** | Execution can succeed while audit fails (a Gem routed correctly but claimed false authority) |\n| **Replaceable parts** | Could swap Router algorithm without touching Provenance logic |\n| **Testable in isolation** | Can test "does routing work?" separately from "does provenance preservation work?" |\n| **Optional enforcement** | Could disable origin checking and execution would still work (audit would just be skipped) |\n| **No data coupling** | Router never reads Provenance; Validator never reads GemSpec |\n\n---\n\n## **What It\'s NOT**\n\n**Orthogonal ≠ Irrelevant**\n\nThe axes are independent BUT both matter:\n- **Without execution:** Nothing happens (no artifacts to track)\n- **Without audit:** Execution happens but you don\'t know who did what\n\nThey\'re separate concerns that must **both be present** for the system to work safely.\n\n---\n\n## **The Architectural Diagram**\n\n```\nExecution flows horizontally → → → →\n                    ↓ (every step gets wrapped)\nProvenance audit flows vertically ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓\n    \n    Input Artifact\n       ↓ (Route by capability)\n    [EXECUTION DECIDES: Which Gem?]\n       ↓ (Validator intercepts)\n    [AUDIT CHECKS: Origin metadata?]\n       ↓\n    Routed to Gem\n       ↓ (Work happens, output created)\n    [EXECUTION SUCCEEDS/FAILS]\n       ↓ (Validator intercepts again)\n    [AUDIT CHECKS: Authority claim valid?]\n       ↓\n    Handoff to recipient\n```\n\n**Same flow.
